title: zsh emits \e[K after every completion-listing row; zshrs emits none

spec.completer:
#compdef fzc9999

local curcontext="$curcontext" state state_descr line ret=1
typeset -A opt_args

_arguments  \
  '1:c:((a\:"add files to archive" b\:"benchmark"))' && ret=0

return ret

observed.notes: Both grids render identically, so only --strict-stream sees it. zsh terminates each listing row with an erase-to-end-of-line; zshrs writes the row and stops. Visible on a terminal only when the row overwrites longer stale text.

variants.note: second witness, confirmed 2026-08-30: a zero-match listing (a _message plus an empty compadd group). Same shape: zsh emits \e[K after 'no matches here, only a message' and after 'a message for an empty group'; zshrs emits neither.

spec.completer:
#compdef fzcc

local expl
_message -r 'no matches here, only a message'
compadd -J g -x 'a message for an empty group' -U -Q -E 2 --

zshrs_binary.kind: debug build under target/ (NOT the Homebrew-installed zshrs)

zsh_binary.note: Homebrew zsh 5.9.2, which is what `zsh` on PATH resolves to here; /bin/zsh is an older build and is NOT what any harness runs.

confirmed.note: round 6 re-confirmation, from the full gate run in tests/compsys_fixtures/last_gate.json. What that run established: verdict STILL-DIVERGES; the harness's own detail was 'raw escape streams differ'; this harness computes no fingerprint, so what was re-verified is the verdict and that detail line, not row-for-row identity with `observed`

history.note: all three harness files had uncommitted edits when this was confirmed (three agents were editing them concurrently); the sha256 prefixes above pin the exact bytes used.
